units.text: INT. SUPERMAN - CONTINUOUS

You need not go begging for my regard. How unreal our moral judgments are! You seem to me to have absolutely no conscience--only hypocrisy; and you can't see the difference--yet there is a sort of fascination about you. I always attend to you, somehow. I should miss you if I lost you.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: tranquilly slipping her arm into his and walking about with him.
But isn't that only natural, Jack? We have known each other since we were children. Do you remember?
units.name: ANN

units.text: abruptly breaking loose.
Stop! I remember EVERYTHING.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Oh, I daresay we were often very silly; but--
units.name: ANN

units.text: I won't have it, Ann. I am no more that schoolboy now than I am the dotard of ninety I shall grow into if I live long enough. It is over: let me forget it.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Wasn't it a happy time?
units.name: ANN

units.text: She attempts to take his arm again.
Sit down and behave yourself.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: He makes her sit down in the chair next the writing table.

No doubt it was a happy time for you. You were a good girl and never compromised yourself. And yet the wickedest child that ever was slapped could hardly have had a better time. I can understand the success with which you bullied the other girls: your virtue imposed on them. But tell me this: did you ever know a good boy?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Of course. All boys are foolish sometimes; but Tavy was always a really good boy.
units.name: ANN

units.text: struck by this.
Yes: you're right. For some reason you never tempted Tavy.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Tempted! Jack!
units.name: ANN

units.text: Yes, my dear Lady Mephistopheles, tempted. You were insatiably curious as to what a boy might be capable of, and diabolically clever at getting through his guard and surprising his inmost secrets.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: What nonsense! All because you used to tell me long stories of the wicked things you had done--silly boys tricks! And you call such things inmost secrets: Boys' secrets are just like men's; and you know what they are!
units.name: ANN

units.text: obstinately.
No I don't. What are they, pray?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Why, the things they tell everybody, of course.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Now I swear I told you things I told no one else. You lured me into a compact by which we were to have no secrets from one another. We were to tell one another everything, I didn't notice that you never told me anything.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: You didn't want to talk about me, Jack. You wanted to talk about yourself.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Ah, true, horribly true. But what a devil of a child you must have been to know that weakness and to play on it for the satisfaction of your own curiosity! I wanted to brag to you, to make myself interesting. And I found myself doing all sorts of mischievous things simply to have something to tell you about. I fought with boys I didn't hate; I lied about things I might just as well have told the truth about; I stole things I didn't want; I kissed little girls I didn't care for. It was all bravado: passionless and therefore unreal.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: I never told of you, Jack.
units.name: ANN

units.text: No; but if you had wanted to stop me you would have told of me. You wanted me to go on.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: flashing out.
Oh, that's not true: it's NOT true, Jack. I never wanted you to do those dull, disappointing, brutal, stupid, vulgar things. I always hoped that it would be something really heroic at last.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Recovering herself.

Excuse me, Jack; but the things you did were never a bit like the things I wanted you to do. They often gave me great uneasiness; but I could not tell on you and get you into trouble. And you were only a boy. I knew you would grow out of them. Perhaps I was wrong.
units.name: ANN

units.text: sardonically.
Do not give way to remorse, Ann. At least nineteen twentieths of the exploits I confessed to you were pure lies. I soon noticed that you didn't like the true stories.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Of course I knew that some of the things couldn't have happened. But--
units.name: ANN

units.text: You are going to remind me that some of the most disgraceful ones did.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: fondly, to his great terror.
I don't want to remind you of anything. But I knew the people they happened to, and heard about them.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Yes; but even the true stories were touched up for telling. A sensitive boy's humiliations may be very good fun for ordinary thickskinned grown-ups; but to the boy himself they are so acute, so ignominious, that he cannot confess them--cannot but deny them passionately. However, perhaps it was as well for me that I romanced a bit; for, on the one occasion when I told you the truth, you threatened to tell of me.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Oh, never. Never once.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Yes, you did. Do you remember a dark-eyed girl named Rachel Rosetree?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: Ann's brows contract for an instant involuntarily.

I got up a love affair with her; and we met one night in the garden and walked about very uncomfortably with our arms round one another, and kissed at parting, and were most conscientiously romantic. If that love affair had gone on, it would have bored me to death; but it didn't go on; for the next thing that happened was that Rachel cut me because she found out that I had told you. How did she find it out? From you. You went to her and held the guilty secret over her head, leading her a life of abject terror and humiliation by threatening to tell on her.
units.name: TANNER

units.text: And a very good thing for her, too. It was my duty to stop her misconduct; and she is thankful to me for it now.
units.name: ANN

units.text: Is she?
units.name: TANNER

units.text: She ought to be, at all events.
units.name: ANN

units.text: It was not your duty to stop my misconduct, I suppose.
units.name: TANNER
